Senses.PreferredTarget: the buddhas and patriarchs from antiquity
Senses.Note: The phrase can honor, test, or overturn inherited authority depending on the present speaker’s scene.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB311.xml). Complete Record of Chan Master Juelangsheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄). Speaker: Juelang Daosheng. After testing a monk in a public address, Juelang says a local land spirit can account for the innumerable encounters of the earlier buddhas and patriarchs, yet fails on a single old Yunmen answer about the meaning of coming from the West. Juelang then tells a comic story of the spirit’s misunderstanding and warns the assembly not to bury the patriarchal point under idle explanation. The phrase names the inherited body of cases being contrasted with one stubborn encounter.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 34–120) (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)). Speaker: Ying'an Tanhua. In a hall address he says the buddhas and patriarchs of old could not state or pull out the matter, whereas he will show it to his listeners. He immediately tests people who label his staff a staff, and those who refuse to call it one, saying both remain shackled at his gate. The phrase marks revered predecessors as a foil for his present demonstration.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師乃云：善言言者，言所不能言；善迹迹者，迹所不能迹。言迹既盡，猶是就理變通，向衲僧門下未足觀光。是故從上佛祖提持正印、密付要旨，若不具別緇素，大眼目如何跂及？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1359.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ying’an Tanhua (應菴曇華禪師語錄). Speaker: Ying'an Tanhua. At the opening of his Mingguo hall, after a monk’s questions and replies, Ying’an says good speech speaks what words cannot say and good traces trace what signs cannot mark. He then invokes the earlier buddhas and patriarchs as bearers of the authentic seal and subtle charge, demanding eyes able to distinguish it. He next raises the Buddha’s flower and Kasyapa’s smile to press the audience on transmission.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：從上佛祖用處，如前日暴風卒雨、迅雷擊電，威靈氣焰不知自何而來，見者無不駭愕。及乎少頃，風休雨霽，青天白日，人皆見其清明，不知許多威靈氣焰又向什麼處去？這般用處，山僧也有些子不欲妄通消息。待後次暴風卒雨之時，汝等諸人急須著眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1376.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chijue Daochong (痴絕道冲禪師語錄). Speaker: Chijue Daochong. In a hall address he compares how the old buddhas and patriarchs worked to a sudden violent storm, thunder and lightning: witnesses are startled, but afterward the sky clears and they cannot say where the force went. He says he has some of that function too, will not describe it idly, and urges listeners to watch when the next storm comes. The phrase points to the predecessors’ active teaching methods, not simply their historical list.

Occurrences.Kwic: 記得。先師高峯和尚三十年深居此山。每以一箇萬法歸一一歸何處話。教人默默提起密密咨叅。但不使間斷。亦不為物境之所遷流。亦不為順逆愛憎情妄之所障蔽。惟以所叅話頭蘊之于懷。行也如是叅。坐也如是叅。叅到用力不及處留意不得時。驀忽打脫。方知成佛其來舊矣。這一著子是從上佛祖了生脫死之已驗三昧。惟貴信得及久遠不退轉。更無有不獲其相應者。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B25/B25n0145.xml). Extensive Record of Zhongfeng Mingben of Tianmu (天目中峰廣錄). Speaker: Zhongfeng Mingben. Addressing a visiting royal party, Zhongfeng recalls how his teacher Gaofeng had students carry the “all things return to one” question continuously through walking and sitting until it broke open. Zhongfeng calls that move the tested absorption by which the earlier buddhas and patriarchs ended birth and death, and urges enduring confidence in it. The X64 version repeats this same address; the author’s own B25 record is retained.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB174.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Juelangsheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師語錄). Speaker: Juelang Daosheng. In a New Year’s Eve hall verse he pictures a figure in iron trousers advancing one staff blow at a time, striking root ignorance and knocking over the earlier buddhas and patriarchs. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB202.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄). Speaker: Baichi Xingyuan. At a hall address occasioned by Xu Siquan’s tonsure during illness and the conversion of his home into a hermitage, Baichi says the new monk should take up wisdom and patience, cut through delusion and affliction, and walk shoulder to shoulder with the buddhas and patriarchs of old. The phrase gives the newly ordained person a model of equal participation, not a distant historical catalogue.

Senses.Explanation: The buddhas and patriarchs of old are the collective predecessors invoked as the Chan lineage’s exemplars. Juelang Daosheng contrasts their many encounters with a land spirit’s inability to grasp one Yunmen case, then in a different New Year’s verse imagines knocking them all over. Ying’an Tanhua first sets his staff demonstration against what earlier buddhas and patriarchs could not state, and in another address names them as transmitters of the authentic seal. Chijue Daochong compares their teaching function to a sudden storm. Zhongfeng Mingben calls continuous investigation of a question their tested path beyond birth and death. Baichi Xingyuan tells a newly ordained householder to walk shoulder to shoulder with them. The phrase locates an inherited authority that each speaker can invoke, challenge, or claim to share.

Occurrences.Kwic: 情識摶量，便為高見，此大病也。從上來事，本無如是。巖頭云：只露目前些子箇。如擊石火、閃電光，若明不得，不用疑著。此是向上人行履處，除非知有，莫能知之。趙州喫茶去，祕魔擎杈，雪峰輥毬，禾山打鼓，俱胝一指，歸宗拽石，玄沙未徹，德山棒，臨際喝，並是透頂透底，直截剪斷葛藤，大機大用，千差萬別，會歸一源，可以與人解黏去縛。若隨語作解，即須與本分草料。譬如十斛驢乳，只以一滴師子乳滴之，悉皆迸散。要脚跟下傳持，相繼綿遠，直須不徇人情，勿使容易，乃端的也。末後一句，始到牢關。誠哉是言，透脫死生，提持正印，全是此箇時節。惟是蹋著向上關捩子者，便諳悉耶。法王沖長老法王沖長老從上宗乘，高超直證，師資契會，斷不等閑。所以二祖立雪斷臂，黃梅負舂，自餘服勤三十二十載，豈容易印可哉。蓋觀機逗教，百煅千煉，纔有偏執疑情，盡為決破，俾徹底放下得平穩，履踐轉換到撲不破之地，如皮可漏子相似，禁當得然後放出，接物利生。此非小小因緣，纔一不周，即模子不正，脫得出來，七凹八凸，取笑作者。是故古德唯務周正，八面玲瓏，內於己行持潔清如冰玉，外則圓通謳和覧群情善回互如陂澤。立參之際，一一以本分事敲點，待其領略，即放手段與琢磨。譬如一器水傳一器，切忌滲漏其間，驅耕奪飢，神鬼莫測，只憑仗一大解脫，更不生異類相中頭角，妥貼無為，真五戒十善出塵阿羅漢也。達磨有言：行解

Occurrences.Kwic: 著草鞋出去也。山曰：此子已後向孤峯頂上盤結草菴，呵佛罵祖去在。師一日齋遲，自托鉢過堂。時雪峰為典座，曰：鐘未鳴，鼓未響，托鉢甚處去？師便歸方丈。峰舉似岩頭，頭曰：大小德山未會末後句。師聞，令侍者請巖至，謂曰：汝不肯老僧那？巖密啟其意。次日上堂，便與尋常不同。巖於僧堂前撫掌曰：且喜堂頭老漢會末後句。雖然，也只得三年。後三年，果遷化。示眾曰：汝但無心於事、無事於心，自然虗而靈、空而妙。若毫端許言之本末者，皆為自欺。何故？毫𨤲繫念，三途業因；瞥爾情生，萬劫羈鎻。聖名凡號，總是虗聲；殊相劣形，皆為妄色。汝欲求之，得無累乎？及其厭之，又成大患，終無所益。雪峯問師：從上宗乘事，某甲還有分也無？師曰：道甚麼？峯有省。廓侍者問：從上諸聖向甚處去？師曰：作麼，作麼？廓曰：勑點飛龍馬，跛鱉出頭來。師休去。來日浴出，廓度湯與師，師撫背云：昨日公案如何？廓曰：者老漢今日方始瞥地。師休去。師一日同瓦棺入山斫木，師將一椀水與棺，棺接得便喫。師曰：會麼？棺曰：不會。師又將一椀水與棺，棺接得又喫。師曰：會麼？棺曰：不會。師曰：何不成褫取不會底？棺曰：不會，又成褫箇什麼？師曰：子大似箇鐵橛。師隔江見高亭，云：不審。師乃搖扇招之，高亭開悟，便橫趍而去。師凡住院，拆却佛殿，獨存法堂而已。贊曰：擔鈔走南方，擔滅諸魔子。逢臭老婆，點出三心。看小當仁，啞

Occurrences.Kwic: 鑿後英，君子未嘗不深歎息也。靈山一會，自擔雪老人潛輝以來，法雨滂沱，人天欣慰。字兄和尚從楚中歸，繼席茲山，三吳學士翕然響風，無不謂先靈巖儼然如在，而門人此公花藥相隨，深入堂奧，是真得見地諦當者，絕無些子軟煖習氣。余愛之重之，適翠峰虛席，字兄命往住焉。丁丑秋，余乞食過洞庭，見溪流菜葉，知當世有如隱山而聲望並汾州者，即吾海印和尚高臥處也。遂同訪翠峰，抵掌快談，不減昔日金輪峰之舊話，乃出平日頌古暨示語一冊，快讀一過，實足醒目。因念雪竇去翠峰五百餘載，復得繼踵前猷，流風逸韻，今古宛然，一言一句，如擊石閃電，列眼便過，應非即言定旨、滯句迷源可比，不惟覺悟塵勞，真使從上宗乘法印無異。若是通方作者，何妨相共證明？書問書問復聖恩仁和尚復聖恩仁和尚去春遠拜隆儀，准擬周甲之後，理棹入山，一舒情愫。適值江水凍合，不獲遂摳謝之願。改歲以來，晴日甚少，而冷熱不時，賤體無日不病，疏惰如此，罪何可言？其亮我恕我，止有法兄耳。雲山睽隔，音問寥寥，緬懷知己，惟有跂予。昨接手諭，深荷注存，三復之餘，曷勝感駭？大概叢林本來無事，皆因六群搆釁，以致幻出非常，終賴山川效靈，中流砥定，非但山門之幸，凡屬宗黨罔不相安。今為祖父法席長久之祝，有和尚在，誹譽莫忌，憂勞可甘，灼然聖恩一柱，又為海內衲子稱慶無涯矣。敬遣寓子，代申頂謝。首夏清和，惟冀順時珍攝。臨穎神

Occurrences.Kwic: 正宗。先除邪執者。故須因事明理。會妄歸真。真是依妄之真。因情說會。事是從理之事。破執言明。無執而理事俱虛。離情而真妄雙絕。瞖消而空華自謝。念息而幻境俄沈。今依諸聖。於眾生界中。抱教迷宗。蓋非一二。撮其樞要。無先二空。以迷人空故。起我見之愚。受妄生死。以迷法空故。違現量之境。障淨菩提。所以我法俱空。唯從識變。今立第一心法。能變識有三。一第八異熟識變。二第七思量識變。三第六了別境識變。既唯識變。我法皆虛。因此二空。故契會玄。旨以我空故。煩惱障斷。以法空故。所知障消。煩惱障斷故。證真解脫。所知障斷故。獲大菩提。然後行滿因門。心冥果海。則境識俱寂。唯一真空。問。從上宗乘。唯令絕學。單刀直入。教外別傳。何假智慧多聞。廣論性相。言繁理隱。水動珠昏。答。顯宗破執。權拂學路討論。達旨。融通。非離文字解脫。法華經云。若有利根。智慧明了。多聞強識。乃可為說。大凡參玄之士。須具二眼。一己眼明宗。二智眼辯惑。所以禪宗云。單明自己。不了目前。如此之人。只具一眼。理孤事寡。終不圓通。隻翼單輪。豈能飛運。若執只要單刀直入。不用廣參者。則善財初見妙德發明之後。不合遍參法界。故知初後心等。理行同時。所以善財至彌勒佛果圓後。却指再見初友文殊。如先德云。文殊之妙智。宛是初心。普賢之玄門曾無別體。是則理事冥齊於一旨。本末匪越於剎那。曷乃守一疑諸。頓迷

Senses.Explanation: The tradition handed down from earlier generations names the inherited Chan transmission. Yuanwu Keqin connects it with rigorous teacher-student confirmation; Xuefeng Yicun and Huangbo Xiyun ask how one shares in or demonstrates it; Heshan compares contemporary writing with its seal; other questioners contrast it with doctrinal learning or ask why it later divided into schools.

Entries.SourceTerm: 從上相承底事，如何指示於人

Senses.PreferredTarget: The matter handed down from the ancients: how do you show it to people?
SearchAliases: The matter handed down from the ancients: how do you show it to people?
Senses.Note: One inherited Huangbo–Baizhang exchange is preserved inside three distinct present appraisals: Hongzhi, Hanyue and Wansong. Wansong's two transported hits continue the same case and are counted once; the fuller explanatory window is retained. X66 copies the old dialogue and Hongzhi's appraisal and is reserve. Huangbo is the original questioner, Baizhang its respondent, and later teachers are present interpreters. No global exhaustion is claimed.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J32/J32nB272.xml). At evening instruction Hongzhi Zhengjue raises Huangbo's question about showing the inherited matter, Baizhang's seated response, the further question about later descendants and Baizhang's departure. Hongzhi credits Baizhang with speech and conduct free of fault and says Huangbo already knows, asking deliberately so that the exchange may circulate widely. He then asks whether the assembly understands Baizhang's returning to his room and answers with falling leaves and autumn water and sky. Huangbo voices the selected question; Hongzhi interprets its testing function.

Occurrences.Kwic: 江西，而大師已化。詣石門禮塔，時大智廬於塔傍，蘗即禮塔。見丈，乃問：願聞平昔得力言句。丈舉一喝三日耳聾話，至一喝處，蘗不覺吐舌退。後丈知已徹，問：子以後莫承嗣馬大師不？蘗曰：不然。今日因師舉，得見馬祖大機大用，且不識馬祖。若嗣馬祖，以後喪我兒孫。丈曰：見與師齊，減師半德；見過於師，方堪傳授。子甚有超師之見。又道：後代兒孫將何傳授？萬松道：千年無影樹，今時沒底靴。黃蘗屢發此語，可謂老覺情多念子孫，可惜百丈有頭無尾。我若見道：後代兒孫將何傳授？却祇以踞坐示之。不然，拽拄杖打出，兒孫也未到斷絕。雖然，他幾曾放過來道：將為你是箇人。百丈踞坐處，諸方認為默然良久。天衣懷云：維摩不默不良久，踞坐商量成過咎。吹毛匣裏冷光生，外道天魔皆斬首。蘗問：從上相承底事，如何指示於人？百丈不曾道著一字，又不曾拈鎚竪拂。天童却道：言滿天下無口過，行滿天下無怨惡。可謂不萌枝上，解辨春秋。黃蘗知而故問百丈：轉見分明，還見百丈、天童轉側處麼？行到水窮處，坐看雲起時。第六十二則仰山問僧第六十二則仰山問僧舉：仰山問僧：近離甚麼處？僧云：廬山。仰山云：曾到五老峰麼？僧云：不曾到。仰云：闍黎不曾遊山。雲門云：祇為慈悲之故，有落草之談。天童拈云：雲門雖然識得仰山底裏，爭奈祇知其一，不知其二。且道仰山意作麼生？無限風流慵賣弄，免人指點好郎君。師云：仰山小釋迦勘僧，雲門僧中王刷欠。這僧實從廬山來，五老峰前蹉過。仰山肚裏歔破脚，尚道不曾遊山。雲門笑他草裏行，不覺自身泥裏走。雲門拈道：這僧親從廬山來，因甚麼却道闍黎不曾遊山？萬松道：幾乎
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1307.xml). In Wansong Xingxiu's commentary on the Huangbo case, he traces the relationship with Baizhang and returns to the question of what later descendants will receive. Wansong says he himself would show the same seated posture or drive the questioner out with his staff, without cutting off the descendants. He rejects the common reading of Baizhang's sitting as mere silence or a long pause, and says Huangbo knowingly asked to bring the matter out more clearly. This fuller continuation supplies Wansong's own interpretation; the earlier transported hit belongs to the same case commentary, not another independent family.

Senses.Explanation: Huangbo asks Baizhang how the inherited matter is shown to others. Baizhang sits in place; Huangbo presses what later descendants will receive, and Baizhang dismisses the premise before returning to his room. Later teachers make the question work again by interpreting that sitting and departure, striking a staff, or offering a different response. Transmission is tested in the encounter, rather than described as an object passed between people. At evening instruction Hongzhi Zhengjue raises Huangbo's question about showing the inherited matter, Baizhang's seated response, the further question about later descendants and Baizhang's departure. Hongzhi credits Baizhang with speech and conduct free of fault and says Huangbo already knows, asking deliberately so that the exchange may circulate widely. He then asks whether the assembly understands Baizhang's returning to his room and answers with falling leaves and autumn water and sky. Huangbo voices the selected question; Hongzhi interprets its testing function. At a hall talk in his Sanfeng record, Hanyue Fazang raises the same question and Baizhang's seated response and withdrawal. Instead of giving a prose explanation, Hanyue speaks of past Buddhas, present bodhisattvas and future students entering or relying upon this gate. He then strikes his staff down and dismisses other miscellaneous affairs as causes of birth and death. The inherited question is Huangbo's; Hanyue's quotation, staff action and concluding exclusion make a separate present application of the exchange. Senses.Explanation: A steward and two teachers use the same assurance in three different encounters. The monastery steward Fangrong presents a verse to Zhuanyu Heng. After the teacher asks whether Fangrong gained his insight while living in the mountains, Fangrong replies that it has never been lacking. The teacher then presses him about where Avalokitesvara is now, and Fangrong answers with images of snow and flowing water. At Hansong Cao’s hall, the teacher answers a sequence of questions about ten kinds of sameness. To the sixth, concerning complete possession, he says that it has never been lacking. At Lingji’s hall, a layman asks why the teacher does not shave his long hair. Lingji gives the same words as his reply, then challenges the visitor’s insistence on distinguishing monks from laypeople. The saying asserts sufficiency, while each exchange tests what that means locally.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X78/X78n1554.xml). Praise of the Orthodox Lineage of the Five Houses. Shitou Xiqian praises Yaoshan's sitting with the verse that begins, 'We have always lived together without knowing its name; we go along together as it happens.' Asked what he is doing, Yaoshan says he does not do a single thing, rejects calling it idle sitting because that would be doing something, and says even sages do not know what is not done. Shitou's full verse likewise denies that either ancient worthies or hasty ordinary people can identify the unnamed companion. The old exchange tests the label of inactivity; it does not establish a separate hidden being that the reader must give a name.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu quotes the exchange and says that even idle sitting cannot be established, much less confused sleepiness, agitation and wandering thoughts. He then comments on Shitou's verse line by line: where could its name be known, even going along naturally remains a hired laborer's condition, and the denial of ordinary understanding is not simply demeaning a respectable person. He asks whether the assembly now knows. His close reading keeps the inherited phrase from becoming an easy recommendation to drift along or merely sit inertly.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB400.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhikongyun. Opening a retreat, Zhikong Xueyun says his assembly is gathered for the same great matter that brought the Buddha into the world. He contrasts an older account of past, present and future practitioners with his own plain lines about poverty making a vegetable meal difficult and busyness leaving no time for cursive writing, then voices Shitou's inherited verse. If the assembly accepts this, he promises accord within the retreat's fifty-three days; if doubt has not opened, he offers another extended teaching on nature and activity. The pair is revoiced in his current instruction, not evidence that the whole assembly has already completed the matter.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1357.xml). Essentials of the Mind by Chan Master Foguo Keqin. Yuanwu Keqin retells Shitou and Yaoshan's exchange and verse, then asks whether this is not someone who has thoroughly verified it: words, verbal devices and measurements do not bind such a person. Conversely, if the ground is unclear and something remains in one's breast, a question is like dragging a cat across felt. The original verse supports Yuanwu's contrast between free response and obstructed handling under questioning. It is not simply praise of lacking a name or refusing to speak.

Xueyan Zuqin praises the Shitou-Yaoshan meeting as a needle and mustard seed fitting without a hair's gap, or two mirrors facing with no trace left behind, but immediately says it still endangers his descendants. He would strike at Yaoshan's first claim to do nothing and calls the later questioning washing earth in mud. He demands that the assembly inspect where Yaoshan establishes his life, then gives his own verse of ordinary sitting and walking, unintentional clouds and mirrors with no person established. The old unnamed-companion verse remains quoted Shitou; Xueyan's counterhandling resists making its smooth mutual understanding an untouchable model.

Shitou's full verse likewise denies that either ancient worthies or hasty ordinary people can identify the unnamed companion. The old exchange tests the label of inactivity; it does not establish a separate hidden being that the reader must give a name. Tianyin Yuanxiu quotes the exchange and says that even idle sitting cannot be established, much less confused sleepiness, agitation and wandering thoughts. He then comments on Shitou's verse line by line: where could its name be known, even going along naturally remains a hired laborer's condition, and the denial of ordinary understanding is not simply demeaning a respectable person. He asks whether the assembly now knows. His close reading keeps the inherited phrase from becoming an easy recommendation to drift along or merely sit inertly. Opening a retreat, Zhikong Xueyun says his assembly is gathered for the same great matter that brought the Buddha into the world. He contrasts an older account of past, present and future practitioners with his own plain lines about poverty making a vegetable meal difficult and busyness leaving no time for cursive writing, then voices Shitou's inherited verse. If the assembly accepts this, he promises accord within the retreat's fifty-three days; if doubt has not opened, he offers another extended teaching on nature and activity. The pair is revoiced in his current instruction, not evidence that the whole assembly has already completed the matter. Yuanwu Keqin retells Shitou and Yaoshan's exchange and verse, then asks whether this is not someone who has thoroughly verified it: words, verbal devices and measurements do not bind such a person. Conversely, if the ground is unclear and something remains in one's breast, a question is like dragging a cat across felt. The original verse supports Yuanwu's contrast between free response and obstructed handling under questioning. It is not simply praise of lacking a name or refusing to speak. Linquan Conglun intersperses comments through the old dialogue, praising a quick turn at 'idle sitting is doing' and Shitou's thorough questioning. At Yaoshan's 'sages do not know,' he imagines even a diamond eye challenged and introduces Shitou's praise as inevitable. Yet he ends by asking where Danxia's cool-eyed observation lies. The pair belongs to Shitou's quoted verse within Linquan's active appraisal; acknowledgment of a close teacher-student fit does not remove the invitation to inspect it from another angle. Xueyan Zuqin praises the Shitou-Yaoshan meeting as a needle and mustard seed fitting without a hair's gap, or two mirrors facing with no trace left behind, but immediately says it still endangers his descendants. He would strike at Yaoshan's first claim to do nothing and calls the later questioning washing earth in mud. He demands that the assembly inspect where Yaoshan establishes his life, then gives his own verse of ordinary sitting and walking, unintentional clouds and mirrors with no person established. The old unnamed-companion verse remains quoted Shitou; Xueyan's counterhandling resists making its smooth mutual understanding an untouchable model.

Senses.Explanation: A capping line that refuses a fixed rank or forced arrangement in several distinct Chan questions. Huanglian Dongyan quotes Gaofeng’s image of one person trapped outside a door and another inside. Rather than devise a technique for their meeting, he lets each enter or leave and ends by saying there has never been a fixed rank to arrange. Yunshan Yan Jushen uses the same line after a long talk on scriptural explanation and the direct transmission; he asks where the extra-scriptural matter lands, strikes his staff, and gives the line. A third source quotes a later teacher named Weishan Guo responding to the old Yunyan father-and-child exchange with the same words. These scenes differ in the puzzle being answered, but the line repeatedly resists imposed order; the Weishan Guo source does not itself settle his full roster identity.

Entries.SourceTerm: 從前汗馬無人識，只要重論盖代功

Senses.PreferredTarget: No one recognized the warhorse’s earlier service; now its unrivaled achievement must be reckoned anew
AlternateTargets: The battle horse’s former toil went unseen; its commanding merit must now be weighed again
SearchAliases: warhorse earlier service unrecognized merit reckoned anew
Senses.Note: The couplet pictures a warhorse whose past service went unrecognized and whose outstanding merit now calls for a fresh reckoning. Several masters use it to reassess an old Chan exchange: Gulin and Juean apply it to Zhaozhou, Shitian to a Guishan dialogue, and Shixi to a meeting of emperor and teacher. Its job is to turn apparent familiarity with a case into a renewed judgment of what it achieved.

Occurrences.Kwic: 。冬夜，小參。拈主丈云：烏石嶺頭時時相見，三毬堂下歷歷播揚，格外談冬來事，吉凶卦兆盡現己躬，多不添一絲，少不減一線，只為元無智眼，淪入邪途，隨󳫴運以推移，共陰陽而消長，莫有挨開天地、揑定陰陽底麼？橫主丈云：一冬二冬，叉手當胸。復舉：定山和尚見首座洗衣次，山問：作什麼？首座提起衣，山云：洗底是什麼衣？座云：福州使鐵錢。定山喚維那移下挂搭，拈云：雪峰從來扶弱不扶強，偏愛斷者公案。定山機鋒少密，平地起堆；首座浣濯自如，辱而不屈。謝兩堂，秉拂，上堂。洞山首座喫菓子，開口落空亡；雪嶠兩堂吞栗蓬，分頭張意氣。衲僧家手是秤、眼是秤，輕也知、重也知，半斤八兩毫髮無虧。雖然，爭奈未明三八九，難辨力㘞希。擊拂，下座。正月城歸，上堂：金烏飛，玉兔馳。歸來重會面，動是隔年期。鼻頭垂下元如舊，三昧依前各不知。散經，上堂。舉：昔有婆子請趙州轉藏，州遶禪床一匝，傳語云：轉藏已竟。婆云：比來請轉全藏，如何只轉半藏？拈云：趙州轉藏，動必全真；婆子開緘，語驚時聽。從前汗馬無人識，只要重論盖代功。十一月旦，上堂：傍家覔佛，著相參禪，何異釣魚於山上，聽水於爐邊？三冬今去，一眨眼，過殘年，翻思少室庭前雪，惟有神光得正傳。謝承天并法石，上堂。迦葉倒剎竿，熱謾慶喜；玄沙乞主丈，鈍置雪峰。爭似我與承天、法石相會，不倒剎竿，不付主丈，一見各自西東。何故如此？恐貽知己哂，盡在不言中。西禪栢堂和尚至，上堂：兩淛江頭屢呈烟棹，大溈堂上又展泥盤。得處深，用處活，中峰直下兒孫，必竟出場自別。別底事作麼生？卓主丈，云：君子可八。謝前堂豐山首座，上堂：人天眼目，佛祖淵源。如合浦夜光，水澄即現；似豐山九耳，霜降即鳴。若論快便難逢，由是未忘所待。莫有不因光而自現、不因鳴而自聞底麼？乃云：三生六十劫。涅槃，上堂。釋尊初出世時，將那一著對天地指注了也？及至後來収拾不上，却道：始從鹿野苑，終至䟦提河，於是二中間，未甞談一字。瞞得阿誰？既曰：我寧不說法，疾入於涅槃？又乃胸摩卍字，槨示双趺，熟睡饒譫語。此等膏肓之疾作麼生醫？若也醫得，便見桃紅李白，真體湛然。其或拱手相看，過去久矣。觀音生日提綱。洪鐘在󱒞，大扣大鳴，小扣小鳴；皓月當空，東來東照，西來西照。猶如菩薩入三摩地，現諸色身，慈眼視眾生，福聚海無量。拈主丈，召眾云：者箇是主丈子，那箇是觀音？且聽雪峰

Occurrences.Kwic: 箇消息麼？古人恁麼說話，意在於何？直饒聞得，暗地点頭，未免死在句下。須知古今山河、古今天地、古今人倫、古今日月，毫髮下移，塵劫來事盡在而今。且而今事作麼生？良久，云：九九陽生第一爻。復舉：趙州會下有僧參相，推不肖作第一座。主事白州，州云：總教作第二座。事云：第一座教誰做？州云：裝香著。事裝香了，白州，州云：戒香、定香、惠香、解脫香。師拈云：趙老應機，如風吹水，第一座香烟起，驢年夢見汗臭氣。冬節，晝明夜暗，日往月來，一氣不然而然，萬化無作而作，便恁麼去，平地上死人無數。衲僧用處，自有條章，斗轉星移，東湧西沒。豈不見溈山問仰山：仲冬嚴寒秊秊事，󳫴運推移事若何？仰山近前叉手立，脚下如漆。溈山云：我情知你答這話不得，父為子隱。香嚴云：某甲偏答得這話，家富小兒嬌。溈山遂問：仲冬嚴寒秊秊事，󳫴運推移事若何？香嚴亦近前叉手而立，果然別有長處。溈山云：賴遇寂子不會，欲隱彌露。溈山恁麼提持，二子恁麼酬對，石田恁麼指注，還當得宗乘中事麼？良久，云：從前汗馬無人識，只要重論盖代功。舉：定山首座洗衣次，山問：作什麼？首座提起衣，山云：洗底是什麼衣？座云：福州使䥫錢。定山喚維那移下挂搭。師拈云：定山可謂借手行拳，一時氣槩；首座雖則失錢遭罪，千古風流。若是石田當時待定山道：洗底是什麼衣？以手掬水便潑，便是千箇。定山未免一場懡㦬。冬節。釋迦不說說，迦葉不聞聞。利劒斬虗空，萬象鳴嚗嚗。便恁麼去，承虗接響，數若塵沙。謝家人不在漁船，錯認橘皮喚作火。所以道，宗門深奧，酌度胸襟。麤飡易飽，細嚼難飢。若是英靈上士，飜轉䥫面皮，竪亞摩醯眼。萬仞崖頭，騰身撲不碎。須彌那畔，招手喚不回。等閑拈一機，示一境，總在生佛未具已前，日月照臨不到處。群陰消與未消，一陽復與未復，豈干他事。然雖如是，畢鉢岩中，猶有人未肯点頭在。何故？趙璧本無瑕，相如誑秦王。復舉洞山請泰首座喫菓子公案。師拈云：這箇話頭其來久矣，總道首座語不契洞山，所以不得菓子喫，殊不知洞山性命在泰首座手裡。莫有為洞山作主底麼？出來，出來。蔣山今夜要斷不平之事，如無，惱亂春風卒未休。歲夜。金烏急，玉兔速，明而又晦，晦而又明，運行不息，今夜已得成功。拂曉金鷄一聲，舊歲新秊交過，東隣西舍李老張哥爭先慶賀，拜得睞頭，穿衲僧家鉢盂，一日兩度濕，任運騰騰，不知月之大小，不管歲之餘閏

Occurrences.Kwic: 就座。僧問：鶴書來自九重天，象駕崢嶸別冷泉，雙徑烟雲俱改觀，請師一句祝堯年。正與麼時，願聞法要。師云：帝與九齡夢，嵩呼萬歲聲。進云：記得僧問百丈：如何是奇特事？丈云：獨坐大雄峰。此意如何？師云：誰敢䂨額？進云：者僧便禮拜又作麼生？師云：也好膽大。進云：百丈便打，此僧還甘也無？師云：放過不可。進云：古人且置，今日若有人問：如何是奇特事？和尚作麼生對？師云：你莫要捋虎鬚麼？僧禮拜，師云：放你三十棒。師乃舉拂子示眾云：我此法印，為欲利益世間故說。山僧行脚五十年、住持三十載，未甞動著。今日既到凌霄頂𩕳雙徑禪林，與諸人把手同歸，正在此日。以拂子擊禪床云：諸人如是見、如是知、如是信解、如是護持，則山僧入院一場佛事功不浪施，堪報不報之恩，以助無為之化。又擊拂子云：且置是事。復舉：佛照和尚住此山日，孝宗皇帝詔問：世尊入山修道六年而成，所成者何事？佛照奏云：將為陛下忘却。師云：孝宗倒腹傾腸，金湯佛氏；佛照抱頭撮脚，覿面當機則不無。畢竟所成者何事？從前汗馬無人識，只要重論盖代功。上堂，召大眾云：山僧自靈隱來登此山，得與諸人相見，一無所有，只提得一瓶東西磵水、數片南北山雲，今日拈來平等供養。或有箇道：甚處青山無此物，何須特地當人情？只向道：莫恠輕微。久立。上堂。我有一語，在在處處，提起分開，放下揑聚，兩手持來，一手分付。江西曾有言。拍禪床，云：以此箇為主。上堂，舉：馬祖一日令智藏馳書上徑山，山接書開，見一圓相，乃於中下一點封回。國師聞得，乃云：欽師猶被馬師惑。後來雪竇云：雪竇見處，也要諸人共知。祇者馬師當時𦘕出，早自惑也。師云：江西清平世界，輕動干戈。徑山行陣久經，不勞餘力。南陽忍俊不禁，也入一分。雪竇一代拈提，宗師到者裏，却作初行脚時語，也是杭州紙貴。謝兩班，上堂。觀音大士一身有八萬四千母陀羅臂，美則美矣，若做箇偏衫子，向甚處著許多袖口？爭似徑山自有眾務，各出隻手，自然無事不辦。雖然，富嫌千口少。謝監収，上堂。八月初一，好箇消息。積雨報初晴，新凉生八極。禾稻滿田疇，催人早収拾。一顆顆，一粒粒，宜愛惜，莫教遍地成狼籍。直待去年今年、官租私租一時還畢，不妨一飽忘百飢，鼓腹謳歌度殘日。且道歌作麼生謳？快活，快活。山鄉歸，上堂：一月相拋不出門，幾經花縣幾烟村？桑麻影裏炊香早，松竹陰中笑語溫。幽磬朝離迎白日

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 何？慶云：草裏漢。云：挂角後如何？慶云：亂呌喚。云：畢竟如何？慶云：驢事未了，馬事到來。雪竇云：寧可碎身如微塵，終不瞎箇眾生眼。長慶較𬅿子，復云：一般漢設使羚羊未挂角，也似萬里望鄉關。師云：雪竇眼觀東南，意在西北，大小長慶答話也不了，雪峰山裏一千五百人善知識還曾夢見也未？舉僧問巴陵：祖意教意同別？陵云：雞寒上樹，鴨寒下水。僧問睦州：祖意教意同別？州云：青山自青山，白雲自白雲。雪竇云：問既一般，答亦相似，其中有利他自利，瞞人自瞞，若點檢分明，管取解空第一。師云：問既不同，答亦有異。因甚如此？巴陵見雲門，睦州見黃檗。舉趙州示眾云：今夜答話去，有解問者出來。時有僧出，州云：比來拋塼引玉，引得箇墼子。法眼和尚遂乃舉問覺鐵觜：先師意作麼生？覺云：如國家拜將。乃問：甚人去得？時有人出云：某甲去得。云：爾去不得。法眼云：我會也。雪竇云：伶俐漢聞舉，便知落處。然雖如此，放過覺鐵觜。夫宗師語不虗發，出來必是作家，因什麼拋塼引墼？諸禪德要識趙州麼？從前汗馬無人識，只要重論盖代功。師云：老趙州寰中獨據，不動一塵，忽然重整戈矛，便見風行草偃，直得盡大地人冰消瓦解。覺鐵觜云：如國家拜，將甚人去得？云：汝去不得。師云：果然。法眼云：我會也。師云：識什麼好惡？雪竇云：夫宗師語不虗，發出來必是作家，因甚麼拋塼引墼？師云：若不酬價，爭辨真偽？舉：耽源辭國師歸省覲馬祖，於地上作一圓相，展坐具禮拜。祖云：子欲作佛去。源云：某甲不解揑目。祖云：吾不如汝。雪竇云：然猛虎不食其子，爭奈來言不豐。諸人要識耽源麼？只是箇藏身露影漢。師云：耽源大似當門獅子，凜凜神威，大小馬師，元來小膽。雪竄云：要識耽源麼？只是箇藏身露影漢，誰道不驚羣？舉：溈山問仰山：甚處來？山云：田中來。溈云：田中多少人？山插下鍬子，叉手而立。溈云：南山大有人刈茅。山拈得鍬子便行。玄沙云：我當時若見，與踏倒鍬子。鏡清云：不奈船何，打破戽斗。僧問明招：古人意在插鍬處？叉手處？招喚：某甲。僧應諾。招云：還曾夢見仰山麼？雪竇云：諸方老宿咸謂插鍬話奇特也，大似隨邪逐惡。若據雪竇見處，仰山被溈山一問，直得草繩自縛，去死十分。師云：諸方老宿與麼提持，雖則洞徹淵源，要見溈仰父子相投，言氣相合，則未可在。玄沙云：我當時若見，即踏倒鍬子。師云：識法者懼。明招喚僧，僧應諾。招云

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 。冬夜，小參。拈主丈云：烏石嶺頭時時相見，三毬堂下歷歷播揚，格外談冬來事，吉凶卦兆盡現己躬，多不添一絲，少不減一線，只為元無智眼，淪入邪途，隨󳫴運以推移，共陰陽而消長，莫有挨開天地、揑定陰陽底麼？橫主丈云：一冬二冬，叉手當胸。復舉：定山和尚見首座洗衣次，山問：作什麼？首座提起衣，山云：洗底是什麼衣？座云：福州使鐵錢。定山喚維那移下挂搭，拈云：雪峰從來扶弱不扶強，偏愛斷者公案。定山機鋒少密，平地起堆；首座浣濯自如，辱而不屈。謝兩堂，秉拂，上堂。洞山首座喫菓子，開口落空亡；雪嶠兩堂吞栗蓬，分頭張意氣。衲僧家手是秤、眼是秤，輕也知、重也知，半斤八兩毫髮無虧。雖然，爭奈未明三八九，難辨力㘞希。擊拂，下座。正月城歸，上堂：金烏飛，玉兔馳。歸來重會面，動是隔年期。鼻頭垂下元如舊，三昧依前各不知。散經，上堂。舉：昔有婆子請趙州轉藏，州遶禪床一匝，傳語云：轉藏已竟。婆云：比來請轉全藏，如何只轉半藏？拈云：趙州轉藏，動必全真；婆子開緘，語驚時聽。從前汗馬無人識，只要重論盖代功。十一月旦，上堂：傍家覔佛，著相參禪，何異釣魚於山上，聽水於爐邊？三冬今去，一眨眼，過殘年，翻思少室庭前雪，惟有神光得正傳。謝承天并法石，上堂。迦葉倒剎竿，熱謾慶喜；玄沙乞主丈，鈍置雪峰。爭似我與承天、法石相會，不倒剎竿，不付主丈，一見各自西東。何故如此？恐貽知己哂，盡在不言中。西禪栢堂和尚至，上堂：兩淛江頭屢呈烟棹，大溈堂上又展泥盤。得處深，用處活，中峰直下兒孫，必竟出場自別。別底事作麼生？卓主丈，云：君子可八。謝前堂豐山首座，上堂：人天眼目，佛祖淵源。如合浦夜光，水澄即現；似豐山九耳，霜降即鳴。若論快便難逢，由是未忘所待。莫有不因光而自現、不因鳴而自聞底麼？乃云：三生六十劫。涅槃，上堂。釋尊初出世時，將那一著對天地指注了也？及至後來収拾不上，却道：始從鹿野苑，終至䟦提河，於是二中間，未甞談一字。瞞得阿誰？既曰：我寧不說法，疾入於涅槃？又乃胸摩卍字，槨示双趺，熟睡饒譫語。此等膏肓之疾作麼生醫？若也醫得，便見桃紅李白，真體湛然。其或拱手相看，過去久矣。觀音生日提綱。洪鐘在󱒞，大扣大鳴，小扣小鳴；皓月當空，東來東照，西來西照。猶如菩薩入三摩地，現諸色身，慈眼視眾生，福聚海無量。拈主丈，召眾云：者箇是主丈子，那箇是觀音？且聽雪峰

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 箇消息麼？古人恁麼說話，意在於何？直饒聞得，暗地点頭，未免死在句下。須知古今山河、古今天地、古今人倫、古今日月，毫髮下移，塵劫來事盡在而今。且而今事作麼生？良久，云：九九陽生第一爻。復舉：趙州會下有僧參相，推不肖作第一座。主事白州，州云：總教作第二座。事云：第一座教誰做？州云：裝香著。事裝香了，白州，州云：戒香、定香、惠香、解脫香。師拈云：趙老應機，如風吹水，第一座香烟起，驢年夢見汗臭氣。冬節，晝明夜暗，日往月來，一氣不然而然，萬化無作而作，便恁麼去，平地上死人無數。衲僧用處，自有條章，斗轉星移，東湧西沒。豈不見溈山問仰山：仲冬嚴寒秊秊事，󳫴運推移事若何？仰山近前叉手立，脚下如漆。溈山云：我情知你答這話不得，父為子隱。香嚴云：某甲偏答得這話，家富小兒嬌。溈山遂問：仲冬嚴寒秊秊事，󳫴運推移事若何？香嚴亦近前叉手而立，果然別有長處。溈山云：賴遇寂子不會，欲隱彌露。溈山恁麼提持，二子恁麼酬對，石田恁麼指注，還當得宗乘中事麼？良久，云：從前汗馬無人識，只要重論盖代功。舉：定山首座洗衣次，山問：作什麼？首座提起衣，山云：洗底是什麼衣？座云：福州使䥫錢。定山喚維那移下挂搭。師拈云：定山可謂借手行拳，一時氣槩；首座雖則失錢遭罪，千古風流。若是石田當時待定山道：洗底是什麼衣？以手掬水便潑，便是千箇。定山未免一場懡㦬。冬節。釋迦不說說，迦葉不聞聞。利劒斬虗空，萬象鳴嚗嚗。便恁麼去，承虗接響，數若塵沙。謝家人不在漁船，錯認橘皮喚作火。所以道，宗門深奧，酌度胸襟。麤飡易飽，細嚼難飢。若是英靈上士，飜轉䥫面皮，竪亞摩醯眼。萬仞崖頭，騰身撲不碎。須彌那畔，招手喚不回。等閑拈一機，示一境，總在生佛未具已前，日月照臨不到處。群陰消與未消，一陽復與未復，豈干他事。然雖如是，畢鉢岩中，猶有人未肯点頭在。何故？趙璧本無瑕，相如誑秦王。復舉洞山請泰首座喫菓子公案。師拈云：這箇話頭其來久矣，總道首座語不契洞山，所以不得菓子喫，殊不知洞山性命在泰首座手裡。莫有為洞山作主底麼？出來，出來。蔣山今夜要斷不平之事，如無，惱亂春風卒未休。歲夜。金烏急，玉兔速，明而又晦，晦而又明，運行不息，今夜已得成功。拂曉金鷄一聲，舊歲新秊交過，東隣西舍李老張哥爭先慶賀，拜得睞頭，穿衲僧家鉢盂，一日兩度濕，任運騰騰，不知月之大小，不管歲之餘閏

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB428.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mixingren. Mixing Jiren reflects on Mahakasyapa and Ananda’s transmission, asks why Ananda needed further help, and voices the warhorse line before a verse.

Senses.Explanation: Three teachers use the warhorse couplet to press their own judgments about old Chan cases and practice. Tianyin Yuanxiu challenges earlier readings of Wuzu’s three answers by Dahui and Chushi, then closes with the image of a warhorse whose service has gone unrecognized. Hengxiulin Falin places the same couplet after the Pang family’s sayings about difficult and easy practice, before giving his own answer. Mixing Jiren invokes the old transmission from Mahakasyapa to Ananda and asks why Ananda still required another teacher’s help; he turns to the warhorse line before his concluding verse. The couplet is a judgment in three different present teachings, not one old dialogue copied three times.

Entries.SourceTerm: 從前汗馬無人識，秪要重論蓋代功

Senses.PreferredTarget: No one knew the warhorse's old toil; now its peerless achievement needs recounting
AlternateTargets: The battle horse's past service went unseen; now speak again of its unmatched feat
Senses.Note: The warhorse once labored without recognition; the speaker now calls its matchless deed back into view. Huigong and Miaoyun deliver the pair with staff gestures. Yikui uses it after recalling his teacher; Danya and Qizong apply it to inherited cases; Jingting ends a retreat-opening address with it. The military image praises effective service and asks the present assembly to recognize what has already been done.

Occurrences.Kwic: 法眼：「如何是曹源一滴水？」眼云：「曹源一滴水。」韶國師聞之豁然。拈云：「城門失火，殃及池魚。」霍山通禪師初參仰山，山閉目坐，師乃翹起一右足曰：「如是如是，西天二十八祖亦如是，唐土六祖亦如是，和尚亦如是，景通亦如是。」仰山起來打四藤條。拈云：「仰山固有偷天手段，霍山亦有換日作略。雖然恁麼，未免弄巧成拙。」昔有婆子供養一菴主，經二十年，嘗令一二八女子送飯給侍。一日，令女子抱定，曰：「正恁麼時如何？」主曰：「枯木倚寒巖，三冬無暖氣。」女子舉似婆，婆曰：「我二十年秪供養個俗漢。」遂遣出，燒卻菴。拈云：「者僧寒巖獨坐，不知屋外春生；婆子暗地驗人，爭奈玉本無瑕。何故？不見嶺梅深雪裡，雲鬢未梳時。」甘贄行者一日入寺設粥，仍請南泉念誦，乃白椎曰：「請大眾為貍奴白牯念摩訶般若波羅密。」甘拂袖便出。泉粥後問典座：「行者在甚麼處？」座云：「當時便」去。泉打破鍋子。拈云：「行者設粥，太煞賣弄，南泉白椎，因便回向。拂袖便行即且止，且道打破鍋子意作麼生？從前汗馬無人識，秪要重論蓋代功。」南泉因兩堂爭貓，泉提起貓云：「大眾！道得即救取，道不得即斬卻。」眾無對，泉即斬。趙州從外歸，師舉似州，州脫草鞋頂頭上而去，泉云：「子若在，即救得貓」。拈云：「南泉莫邪在握，殺活臨時。趙老雖則機用峻捷，亦是賊後張弓。」鼓山示眾云：「鼓山門下不得咳嗽。」時有僧咳嗽一聲，山云：「作麼？」僧云：「傷風。」山云：「傷風即得。」拈云：「鼓山開門引賊，者僧當面竊取。何故？家有白澤圖，必生如是怪。」僧問雲門：「如何是佛？」門云：「乾矢橛」。拈云：「雲門雖能別展生機，未免口裏出臭，至今令人掩鼻。原上座則不然，或問：『如何是佛？』但云：『破木杓。』且道與雲門是同是別？」頌古頌古靈雲見桃花。頌云：「爛熳春光二月天，靈雲觸著眼皮穿。當時不得玄沙老，爭得佳聲亙古傳。」陸亙大夫謂南泉曰：「肇法師也甚奇怪，解道天地與我同根，萬物與我一體。」泉指牡丹云：「大夫！時人見此一株花，如夢相似。」陸罔措。頌云：「天地同根物不殊，了無形像可名模。南泉指出花如夢，彼一男兒我丈夫。」大巔擯首座。頌云：「春秋多少數難窮，百八輪珠暗裏通。夾岸桃花風雨後，馬蹄何處避殘紅。」臨濟三頓痛棒。頌云：「三度禹門遭點額，一朝觸著便稱尊。爪牙突露威獰甚，攪動山川海嶽昏。」德山入門便棒

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 法眼：「如何是曹源一滴水？」眼云：「曹源一滴水。」韶國師聞之豁然。拈云：「城門失火，殃及池魚。」霍山通禪師初參仰山，山閉目坐，師乃翹起一右足曰：「如是如是，西天二十八祖亦如是，唐土六祖亦如是，和尚亦如是，景通亦如是。」仰山起來打四藤條。拈云：「仰山固有偷天手段，霍山亦有換日作略。雖然恁麼，未免弄巧成拙。」昔有婆子供養一菴主，經二十年，嘗令一二八女子送飯給侍。一日，令女子抱定，曰：「正恁麼時如何？」主曰：「枯木倚寒巖，三冬無暖氣。」女子舉似婆，婆曰：「我二十年秪供養個俗漢。」遂遣出，燒卻菴。拈云：「者僧寒巖獨坐，不知屋外春生；婆子暗地驗人，爭奈玉本無瑕。何故？不見嶺梅深雪裡，雲鬢未梳時。」甘贄行者一日入寺設粥，仍請南泉念誦，乃白椎曰：「請大眾為貍奴白牯念摩訶般若波羅密。」甘拂袖便出。泉粥後問典座：「行者在甚麼處？」座云：「當時便」去。泉打破鍋子。拈云：「行者設粥，太煞賣弄，南泉白椎，因便回向。拂袖便行即且止，且道打破鍋子意作麼生？從前汗馬無人識，秪要重論蓋代功。」南泉因兩堂爭貓，泉提起貓云：「大眾！道得即救取，道不得即斬卻。」眾無對，泉即斬。趙州從外歸，師舉似州，州脫草鞋頂頭上而去，泉云：「子若在，即救得貓」。拈云：「南泉莫邪在握，殺活臨時。趙老雖則機用峻捷，亦是賊後張弓。」鼓山示眾云：「鼓山門下不得咳嗽。」時有僧咳嗽一聲，山云：「作麼？」僧云：「傷風。」山云：「傷風即得。」拈云：「鼓山開門引賊，者僧當面竊取。何故？家有白澤圖，必生如是怪。」僧問雲門：「如何是佛？」門云：「乾矢橛」。拈云：「雲門雖能別展生機，未免口裏出臭，至今令人掩鼻。原上座則不然，或問：『如何是佛？』但云：『破木杓。』且道與雲門是同是別？」頌古頌古靈雲見桃花。頌云：「爛熳春光二月天，靈雲觸著眼皮穿。當時不得玄沙老，爭得佳聲亙古傳。」陸亙大夫謂南泉曰：「肇法師也甚奇怪，解道天地與我同根，萬物與我一體。」泉指牡丹云：「大夫！時人見此一株花，如夢相似。」陸罔措。頌云：「天地同根物不殊，了無形像可名模。南泉指出花如夢，彼一男兒我丈夫。」大巔擯首座。頌云：「春秋多少數難窮，百八輪珠暗裏通。夾岸桃花風雨後，馬蹄何處避殘紅。」臨濟三頓痛棒。頌云：「三度禹門遭點額，一朝觸著便稱尊。爪牙突露威獰甚，攪動山川海嶽昏。」德山入門便棒

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 僧又問：『粗言及細語，皆歸第一義，是否？』子云：『是。』僧云：『喚和尚作頭驢，得麼？』子便打。」師云：「有頭無尾漢，當時何不拗折拄杖，熱面再唾？」舉：「僧問藥山：『平田淺草，麈鹿成群，如何射得塵中主？』山云：『看箭。』僧放身便倒。山云：『侍者拖出。』僧便走。山云：『弄泥團漢有甚麼限？』」師云：「雖似見機而作，卻也隈刀避劍。若解當鋒取勝，果然是員戰將。」舉：「梁武帝問達磨：『如何是聖諦第一義？』磨云：『廓然無聖。』帝云：『對朕者誰？』磨云：『不識。』帝不契，磨乃渡江至魏。」師云：「祖師純剛打就，武帝生鐵鎔成，驀劄相逢，佳話千古。雖然如是，門庭施設即不無，若約衲僧門下，須別有振作始得。諸人脫或遲疑，山僧不免別行一路去也。」呵呵大笑，下座。舉：「文殊、普賢起佛見法見，世尊以威神力，貶向二鐵圍山。」師云：「有等瞎眼阿師見恁般公案，便道：『動念即乖。』大似狂狗逐塊。真上座見處與諸方各別，如今設有起佛見、法見底，無底缽盂盛飯供養伊。何故聻？從前汗馬無人識，秪要重論蓋代功。」舉三聖透網念鱗因緣。師云：「我即不然。『透網金鱗，未審以何為食？』『木札羹、鐵釘飯。』千五百人善知識，話頭也不識，莫怪空疏，伏惟尚嚮。」頌古頌古舉誰是彌勒、誰云彌勒因緣。誰是彌勒云彌勒，眼睛鼻子俱突出，衲僧撞見眼頭高，盡力提持去不得。舉興教坦和尚開堂因緣。無人識意憶南泉，鼻孔撩天也被穿，等閑運出鐵牛機，華岳三峰倒插天。舉玄沙同天龍斫柴因緣。五五二十五，打破鹽官鼓，覿面絕疏親，特地大家補。大家補，四七二三面相睹。舉德山到溈山因緣。掣電轟雷運略韜，收來放出在秋毫，坐觀成敗溈山老，陷虎機能用不勞。舉：「雪峰示眾云：『盡大地撮來如粟米粒大，拋向面前，漆桶不會，打鼓普請看。』」堪笑雪峰老婆禪，無端拈出教人看，可憐待兔守株客，不解風前聽杜鵑。舉：「僧問洞山：『如何是佛？』山云：『麻三斤。』」如何是佛麻三斤，當陽獨露絕疏親，雖然佛法無多子，倒底還他手眼明。舉：「俱胝凡有僧問，只豎一指。」俱胝佛法不爭多，試問時人見也麼？擬向指頭尖上會，鷂子早已過新羅。舉：「僧問：『寒暑到來，如何迴避？』」迴避寒暑枉勞神，無寒暑處語豈誠？鴛鴦繡出從君看，不把金針度與人。舉：「良禪客問欽山：『一鏃破三關時如何？』山云：『放出關中主看。』良云：『與麼則知過必

Entries.SourceTerm: 從天降下則貧窮，從地涌出則富貴

Senses.PreferredTarget: Descending from heaven brings poverty; springing from the earth brings riches.
SearchAliases: Descending from heaven brings poverty; springing from the earth brings riches.
Senses.Note: The poverty-riches contrast turns on how something arrives. Later questioners separately ask about earth-emerging riches and about heaven-born versus earth-emerging itself, while the robe address tests receiving and relinquishing what is already at hand.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有文殊普賢，住住，我識得你。列祖提綱錄卷第九列祖提綱錄卷第十武林十八㵎理安禪寺住持婁東行悅集五參提綱洞山价禪師。上堂：還有不報四恩三有者麼？眾無對。又曰：若不體此意，何超始終之患？直須心心不觸物，步步無處所，常無間斷，始得相應。直須努力，莫閒過日。上堂：有一人在千人萬人中，不背一人，不向一人，你道此人具何面目？雲居出曰：某甲參堂去。雲居膺禪師上堂，舉先師道：地獄未是苦，向此衣線下不明大事，却是最苦。師曰：汝等既在者箇行流，十分去九，不較多也。更著些子精彩，便是上座不屈平生行脚，不孤負叢林。古人道：欲得保任此事，須向高高山頂立，深深海底行，方有些子氣息。汝若大事未辦，且須履踐玄途。上堂：得者不輕微，明者不賤用，識者不咨嗟，解者無厭惡。從天降下則貧窮，從地涌出則富貴。門裏出身易，身裏出門難。動則埋身千丈，不動則當處生苗。一言迥脫，獨拔當時。言語不要多，多則無用處。上堂：如人將三貫錢買箇獵狗，祇解尋得有蹤跡底。忽遇羚羊挂角，莫道蹤跡，氣息也無。僧問：羚羊挂角時如何？師曰：六六三十六。曰：挂角後如何？師曰：六六三十六。僧禮拜，師曰：會麼？曰：不會。師曰：不見道無蹤跡？上堂：孤迥迥，峭巍巍。僧出問曰：某甲不會。師曰：面前案山子也不會。上堂。僧家發言吐氣。須有來由。莫將等閒。者裏是甚麼所在。爭受容易。凡問箇事。也須識些子好惡。若不識尊卑良賤。不知觸犯。信口亂道。也無利益。傍家行脚。到處覓相似語。所以尋常向兄弟道。莫怪不相似。恐同學太多去。第一莫將來。將來不相似言語。也須看前頭。八十老人入場屋。不是小兒
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X64/X64n1260.xml). Outline Record of the Successive Patriarchs explicitly heads the original hall passage for Yunju Daoying. He says that gaining must not be treated lightly or understanding used cheaply, then gives the heaven-and-earth contrast. He follows it with the difficulty of leaving through the body rather than merely emerging through a door, and warns that both moving and staying still can entangle. The paired formula belongs to this address, not to a new economic maxim supplied by the compiler.

Hansong Zhicao, in Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hansong Cao, quotes Yunju's longer address and praises its joined illumination and function, then objects that it draws a prison on the ground and binds without a rope. He especially presses the difference between leaving through the door and leaving through the body, answering with a stone tiger and jade unicorn. His criticism tests the surrounding teaching rather than repeat the poverty-riches pair as a final explanation.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X64/X64n1260.xml). Outline Record of the Successive Patriarchs explicitly heads the original hall passage for Yunju Daoying. He says that gaining must not be treated lightly or understanding used cheaply, then gives the heaven-and-earth contrast. He follows it with the difficulty of leaving through the body rather than merely emerging through a door, and warns that both moving and staying still can entangle. The paired formula belongs to this address, not to a new economic maxim supplied by the compiler.

Senses.PreferredTarget: What descends from heaven is poor; what rises from the earth is rich
SearchAliases: what descends from heaven is poor; what rises from the earth is rich
Senses.Note: The old saying calls what descends from heaven poor and what rises from the earth rich. Tianyin uses it to ask whether listeners stand in their own understanding or only repeat old ground. Guxue connects the reversal to stepping out of a fixed position, while Guantao refuses borrowed answers. Huitai says he sees neither descent nor emergence before giving a bare-handed response. The line unsettles the expected high and low values rather than ranking sky and earth.

Senses.Explanation: A day-span unit naming the whole stretch from morning to evening — granted, graded, scheduled, and seen through across the records. Yunmen Wenyan throws the whole day open — speak crosswise, speak lengthwise, morning to evening, no one stops your mouth; and not letting you speak, how then? — the grant and the trap in one address, carried in the five-house selection; Ying'an Tanhua grades the thirty-two marks and the eighty adornments — morning to evening they chirp and squeak, talking yellow and black, never knowing where the two periods are; Xueyan Zuqin tells his own young seeking — tonsured at five, walking out at eighteen, spending the ten-direction retreat at the Twin Grove hammer-stake's assembly morning to evening inside the monks' hall, never past the courtyard gate, hands folded at chest, eyes never past three feet; and Gaofeng Yuanmiao, his doubt-mass nailed and glued, unmoved in a crowd as though alone, morning to evening and evening to morning, limpid and towering, pure clarity without a speck, one thought ten thousand years — until the sixth day at the stupa recital the void shatters and the great earth sinks. Zhe'an Jingfan answers the asking after the working point — three meals a day, morning to evening — and, told it is not understood, herding the ox by day and turning the mill by night; Fangrong Ruxi runs the whole schedule aloud — rising, washing, reciting, porridge, field-work, foot-washing, tea, still-sitting, the afternoon past — morning to evening in ordered sitting and walking, plain word and plain silence, every doing this one thing, and any talk of another teaching thrown out as outward chasing with no such fellow under the Yunju gate; Tianran Hanshi opens the retreat with the whole earth the retreat ground and all suns and moons its season — dressing and eating, sweeping and incense, firewood and water, greeting guests, the four peoples' work and the hundred tasks rising, and even the rise and fall of right and wrong inside the square inch, all the retreat's own mind — so what retreat is there left to close?; and Azi Jinwu, who never taught headwords in the room, teaches only this: on the things themselves, through the day's long continuity, see out the one discontinuous — that is your original face, and the held-up flower and the wall-facing one can no longer fool you.

Zhuyu replies that there is not a drop there, and Zhaozhou leans his staff against the wall and leaves. Baichi then comments on how the visit might have gone had Zhuyu answered differently. The movement belongs to Zhaozhou in the quoted case; Baichi supplies the present appraisal.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: Baichi raises the Zhaozhou-Zhuyu encounter; the narration assigns the crossing in both directions to Zhaozhou Congshen.

Senses.Explanation: Crossing from east to west and from west to east describes a doubled walk across a Dharma hall in two raised encounter cases. Kuifu raises Deshan's visit to Weishan: Deshan carries his bundle across the hall in both directions, calls out, starts to leave, then returns to meet Weishan formally. Baichi raises Zhaozhou's visit to Zhuyu: Zhaozhou makes the same traverse, calls it testing the water, and departs after Zhuyu says there is not a drop. Kuifu and Baichi are later teachers who bring the cases before their audiences; Deshan and Zhaozhou are the actors whose movement the phrase records. The wording is physical action in each case, not a fixed symbol for opposing directions.

Senses.Explanation: The downward stroke out of the empty — the counter-move to every step-by-step climb, ruled at the root over Nanquan and turned from the Song incense-seat to the Qing halls. The root sits in Yunmen Wenyan's own room-essence: the monk asks Nanquan — before Ox-head saw the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds offer flowers? stepping step by step on the buddha-stairway; and after seeing, why no offering? even not coming, still a thread short of this Old Wang — and Yunmen rules: Nanquan only knew climbing step by step, not letting down out of the empty; asked what the climbing is, the incense world; asked what the letting-down is, fill the ditches and stop the ravines; Yuanwu Keqin, at night discourse, works the four turns of the true eye — always-not-so, gazing at the Milky Way and no favoring of feelings; always-so, ash-head and earth-face, hauling water and dragging mud; so-within-not-so, leveling the high downward; not-so-within-so, letting down out of the empty — and the one who minds neither: neither light nor dark, neither releasing nor gathering, the frost-night moon falling of itself into the stream ahead; Huqiu Shaolong, at his incense-seat, spends the stroke on his own awakening — thirty years out of one grove and into another treasure-shrine, cheap made dear and dear made cheap, and at the last knocking into the no-faced old man who struck the life-vein, and letting down out of the empty without meaning to — now he cannot but hold it up before all, one stick of incense for his teacher the buddha-fruit Yuanwu of Jinshan, repaying the milk of the way; and Zhongfeng Mingben, after the wisdom-sword that already cost its own life — the king's treasury holds no such knife — rules that here one may indeed let down out of the empty, then go under the elders' bitter tongs to be forged again: three heads and six arms at ease, the tangled old cases bound in one bundle and flung beyond the other worlds, both hands held out empty at the market gate and the lone peak's top, eighteen transformations for the door-leaners to knock their brows at. Miyun Yuanwu turns the stroke against the buddhas of the three eras — not-knowing-there-is, letting down out of the empty; the cat and the ox knowing-there-is, rising from the ground; let down, no beings to ferry; risen, past buddha and past patriarch — past buddha and patriarch, the beings all ferried; the sand-grit buddhas with no being to ferry, what buddha ever ferried one? — and with both ends cut and the middle flung open, the hard-to-tell one line: straw-cloaked, standing aside past the thousand peaks, drawing water to water the greens before the Five Elders; Tian'an Sheng reads the two doomed heroes with it — slander entered, Qu Yuan sank boned in the Xiang; the Cloud-Dream hunt feigned, the Han founder's general bound: pity the two, small men, who only knew climbing step by step and not letting down out of the empty — their folly, not their wisdom; had they known the rare bond under their own heels, wealth to match a kingdom and no kingdom could invade, honor past marquis and king and none could strip it, wisdom the buddhas and patriarchs cannot spy — dwelling in the world's broad dwelling, standing in the world's right place, walking the world's great way; and Sanyi Mingyu, whisk raised, ties the two motions into one breath — rising from the ground into empty sky, and even so you must let down out of the empty: the wind that bears you thick, therefore the waves run wide — and out of one pore of hair, out of a needle's eye, pearls and agate, coral and amber flow with no minding: a treasury that plays at the buddhas' work, lighting worlds and feeding buddhas, the whole flower-treasury ocean in good order.

Senses.Explanation: Three teachers place Guanyin’s inherited practice formula into separate verses and praises of the bodhisattva. Muyun Tongmen composes a short poem on Guanyin, joining hearing, reflection, and practice with entering samadhi, then compares knowing for oneself to tasting water. Shengke Deyu writes a separate praise of Guanyin in which the same phrase leads to the bodhisattva’s responsive aid across the world. Beijian Jujian writes a series of contemplative verses on Guanyin and uses the full formula while turning attention from sound to the stilling of movement. These are distinct present poems invoking the older Guanyin practice tradition, not claims that their authors invented the formula.

Senses.Note: The future seventh ancestor Vasumitra meets Miccaka in a market while carrying a wine vessel. He asks where the teacher comes from and where he wishes to go; Miccaka says, “I come from my own mind and intend to go nowhere.” Their next turns test recognition and the vessel’s apparent impurity before Vasumitra joins him. Jie’an responds to the meeting as an unexpected recognition in the street. Yingning turns to the vessel and the change of allegiance. Zhe’an brings out the strain between going east or west and arriving from mind; Jifei praises the encounter as a break with outward wandering. The same old reply takes different force in these later responses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 發明當人本地風光耳。苟發明矣，不待融會，一一自知下落處，也不是一箇儱侗和同底道理便當得者。佛說一切法，為除一切心，我無一切心，焉用一切法？五宗門庭差別，正除人差別心者，如差別心量未盡，豈可便云焉用？正好於差別中參到無差別底田地，便是本地風光現前底時節。示忘證丁居士示忘證丁居士若欲超生脫死，須向無生死地上著力，得箇證悟始得。既悟矣，則生死之心既破，無生死之地亦空。能證之人既泯，所證之理亦忘。則在生而生，在死而死，總是自家屋裏事。茲因忘證道人乞法語，故書此以示。且如何是忘證底事？撞著道伴交肩過，一生參學事畢。示玅高居士示玅高居士此事人人本具，箇箇圓成，悟與不悟，了無差別。未得入處時，一箇箇頂天立地；既得入處時，一人人鼻直眉橫。所以悟時，正悟此不待悟底，而無悟跡之可尋。香巖云：「一擊忘所知。」仰山云：「悟則不無，爭奈落在第二頭何？」天皇云：「但盡凡情，別無聖解。」正全提無剩之旨。玅高居士既有入處，悟跡難除，二六時中要求箇不間斷，未免反成間斷。須知間斷與不間斷，皆力量未充，自生障礙。如今要得透頂透底，但撒開兩手，放教活卓卓地，不使有不間斷之相現前，自然不見有間斷之相，便是臨別囑付。

Senses.Explanation: Brush shoulders with a companion on the Way, and a lifetime of study is done. An encounter with a true companion can bring the matter to immediate recognition. Current deployments include Shiqi Tongyun in J26nB183, Baichi Xingyuan in J28nB202, Chaozong Tongren in J34nB300, Shanyi Ruchun in J39nB468, and Neishao Zhizhong in J34nB306. The full paired image remains the lexical unit. Several speakers challenge the line, so it is not a promise that any casual meeting finishes practice.

Senses.Explanation: To deceive people is a recurring adverse judgement on words, conduct, or inherited interpretations. The phrase retains that ordinary act while Chan records put it under public pressure. Yunmen asks for a saying that does not deceive people, then supplies the substitute response, “Do not say this is the one that deceives people.” Miyun Yuanwu states that deceiving people is no good affair and that a good affair does not deceive people; Fushi Tongxian publicly raises the positive half. Shiyu Mingfang attacks people who deceive others for gain, while Wuzhun Shifan distinguishes deceiving people from deceiving oneself. In the Blue Cliff Record, Longya Judun denies that patriarchs and buddhas intend deception but says that, because people cannot pass through, they nevertheless become deceivers. The phrase therefore becomes a test of sayings, speakers, hearers, and self-deception without losing its transitive meaning or allowing the entry to infer intent where Longya denies it.

Senses.Explanation: A monk, two teachers, and a commentator use this line in four different tests of seeing. In Yuan'an Feng's hall, the teacher asks the assembly to explain his verse at the end of a session. Several monks offer answers. One says that the least bit cannot be hidden from him, and the teacher eventually strikes a monk before leaving. Hansong Zhicao reads an older dialogue about the moon before and after fullness. He faults its answers and supplies his own alternatives; for the full moon he says that not the least bit can be hidden. Mingjue comments on the famous Mazu and Baizhang whisk encounter. He challenges whether Baizhang truly awakened at Mazu's shout and says a clear-eyed person cannot be deceived in the slightest. Neishao Zhong addresses the ordinary paths through the monastery. He says the corridor, steps and quarters cannot hide anything from the clear eye beneath each person's heels, then lifts and strikes his staff. The line points to separate questions of recognition rather than one repeated event.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB238.xml). During evening service, Chuiwan Guangzhen asks a monk why, already being a monk, he still takes refuge. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB301.xml). At a hall talk requested by layman Zhou, Jiqi Hongchu strikes the staff while speaking of everyone's field and the ancestral coming from the west. He says a white cloud across the valley mouth has confused the source for many, then introduces the headword as a received saying. He asks someone to speak a sentence from the ancestral lifeline and help complete the patron's gratitude offering. After silence he says the talk will circulate widely thirty years later. The quotation sharpens his present request without identifying the saying's original author.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB494.xml). At a birthday hall talk on the second day of the precept assembly, a monk asks why a solitary pine flourishes while other trees wither. Yushan Shangsi asks how long its roots are after the monk claims it is beyond seasons and cultivation. The monk invokes an eye that cannot glimpse it; Yushan replies with the headword. When challenged that he does not understand the topic, Yushan answers that Tianning's abbot is busy, then predicts the monk will complain thirty years later. The rebuke targets this exact chain of elevated phrases.

Senses.Explanation: The line rebukes speech that repeats an established pattern while claiming freedom. Sanyi applies it to imitated answers; Chuiwan answers a monk's self-refuge formula with it; Jiqi quotes it before demanding a fresh sentence; Yushan directs it at a monk's polished account of the solitary pine. The old rut is shown in what the interlocutor actually says, rather than treated as a blanket prohibition on speech. Sanyi Mingyu criticizes people who learn plausible-sounding answers and mistake the capacity to raise a hand or shout for their own realization. His examples run through Zhaozhou's cloth shirt, the dog, lantern and pillar, then questions about hands, feet and one's place of birth. After the conventional answer that the speaker comes from Xiuzhou, Sanyi gives the headword amid images of leaning on walls and weak wings clinging to branches. The clause names the dependence he has just demonstrated in borrowed verbal patterns. During evening service, Chuiwan Guangzhen asks a monk why, already being a monk, he still takes refuge. The monk says there is no harm in taking refuge in himself. Chuiwan answers with the headword; when the monk claims never to have gone out the gate, Chuiwan calls him a clumsy donkey turning a mill. The formula is an immediate rebuke to the student's self-contained explanation. B239 preserves the same exchange and remains a parallel witness, not a second current setting. Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liangting Ting of Yunxi, Liangting Jingting addresses the assembly in a general teaching. He recalls older sayings that a foot of action outweighs a yard of speech and that speaking and doing cannot be traded by verbal cleverness alone. He then says that a phrase must show the speaker’s actual eye rather than be pieced together by ordinary calculation. “If words do not leave the old groove, how can one get out of the binding veils?” is his own warning in that argument. He goes on to discuss Caoshan’s three leaks and warns that a bellyful of marvelous images can become another leak if one clings to the turn. This is not a direct reply to a questioning monk.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baochizong, Baochi Xuanzong first raises the old encounter in which a monk asks Zhaozhou why Bodhidharma came from the West and Zhaozhou twice answers “the cypress tree in the courtyard,” despite the monk’s objection that he should not point to external objects. Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuan’an Feng, Yuan’an Liao criticizes hearers who turn every phrase into a fixed interpretation: talk of ordinary eating becomes “constant,” and dramatic images become “empty.” He asks what a true eye for study or a phrase showing one’s view would be, then mocks stock replies such as pointing below the eyebrows or beside the nose, stepping forward, or raising a fist. “If words do not leave the old groove, how can one get out of the binding veils?” names the failure of those borrowed answers. Yuan’an then asks where the illness lies and says it is the tendency to stick to being, nonbeing, or the extraordinary. His later question leaves the assembly to examine that attachment, rather than supplying another formula.

Senses.Explanation: “If words do not leave the old groove, how can one get out of the binding veils?” challenges speech that repeats a ready-made pattern. Yushan puts it to a monk displaying a polished verse, Liangting uses it in a general warning against verbal skill without enacted understanding, Baochi applies it to an old Zhaozhou case while questioning his own criticism, and Yuan’an Liao uses it against stock answers about study and insight. Each occurrence has a different current setting, though all four test whether words have become merely familiar moves.

Senses.Explanation: Words and phrases, especially the verbal formulations used to teach or discuss Chan. Yuanwu Keqin warns a head monk against binding learners to fixed wording and, in a separate commentary, asks readers to understand before phrases arise. Gulin Qingmao uses the term for a monastery officer’s leading formulations; an unnamed poem praises Xuedou’s poems and phrases while warning against clinging to their verbal surface. Baizhang Huaihai says there are no special phrases to hand over as a separate teaching. Nanquan Puyuan names his past exchanges with Guizong Zhichang before pressing beyond talk, and Shaozhou Cheng Xiying Yue opens a hall verse by denying that his school depends on set phrases. A compiler also uses the word to describe the material lay official Zeng Hui brings to Mingjue.

Entries.SourceTerm: 語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談

Senses.PreferredTarget: Speech carries the mystery but leaves no road; the tongue talks without talking
AlternateTargets: Words hold the subtle point without giving a path; the tongue speaks while not speaking
SearchAliases: speech carries mystery no road tongue talks without talking
mysterious words tongue speaks without speaking
Senses.Note: Jiashan gives this pair when the Boat Monk presses him to speak about casting a line. Words can carry the subtle point, yet they do not lay down a road; the tongue speaks and does not speak. Guting, Faxi, Yezhu, and Baiyu revisit the exchange, while Feiyin and Yingning voice the pair in present teaching. The two halves belong together: the first removes a fixed route through words and the second shows that speech still happens.

Occurrences.Kwic: 任教明月落重臺。法執盡而見地圓，根本脫而理事徹，直窺髻裏玄珠，可別輪王至寶。如《金光明經》云：『如來言三種身：依諸伏道，起事心盡；依法斷道，依根本心盡；依最勝道，根本心盡。起事心滅故，得現化身；依根本心滅故，得顯應身；根本心滅故，得至法身。』既云教外別傳，何使提挈綱宗？假令別有規模，未免斬頭覓活。若果如是，未夢見在；若不如是，未夢見在。急須蕩盡聖凡情見，方能不滯尊貴階梯。如峰著為『秤錘落井又泥深』，斯謂藥石除而反墮膏肓之疾，鉤餌脫而復遭羅網之悲，滯十成之死句、困相似之疑城，見處既帶瓦礫，發言難印宗乘。欲識同時不識之祖父，舉步亂雲迷四野，攜笻無路透孤峰。如頌云：『翻轉青銅鏡背看。』不聞古德云：『向道莫去，歸來背父。』又何許鏡背看也？次云：『硃砂斑厚壙泥乾』，好個摩空句子，不當落在點劃場中。所云：『易分雪裏粉，難辨墨中煤。』當悟綿綿化母之機，寂寂真風一段。峰既將穿密室，何陷顧貯之泥塗，更沒文彩于琢削，豈能絕眾響而豁天真之提唱乎？宜知語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談。又云：『光生不用揩磨舊』，秪如古鏡未磨時，是個甚麼消息？末云：『漢製從來體自圓』，不見寒山道：『無物堪比倫。』峰又用製作麼？無有譬喻能喻此法，總製得圓，早已缺陷了也。將欲古之又古、深之又深，竭力摸寫，逼真得盡，不知弄巧成拙，揀點將來，料掉沒交涉。住！住！既道向亦不是、背亦不是，畢竟如何即是？」一喝，云：「鐵牛撞倒帝釋宮，百億須彌汗如雨。」峰問：「曹山立三種墮，註者言：『師凡言墮，謂混不得、類不齊。』又明安不受食，是尊貴墮。須知那邊了，卻來這邊行履，不虛此位，即墮尊貴矣。且道：曹山三墮意，畢竟是那一種？」峰著云：「從來不借雙關路，鉤鎖中間直下拋。」頌曰：這邊那邊都不得，合水和泥總不知。牛斷鼻繩湖草綠，牧童濃睡月低垂。師著云：「落日海潮夜，秋光腦後看。」頌曰：天水勿違明舊德，群龍無首殫餘知。挾類混然成錯吉，門庭三五不須垂。師荅云：「閒花野草，橫鋪古錦化春工；山色溪光，密布真風超象外。全身入荒草，徐行足跡混塵埃。脅右書半行，獨許狸奴知個事，分明頭角宛轉巴歌。故曹山有三墮之神樞，大珠剖絕向之正受。其法也，如鼎繫足，不煩輕重于其間；似月穿波，忘所合流于徹底。明安復為布置，一以折三、以三冥一，亦不另擬隨類墮之等，則尊貴墮之差殊。故云：

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 喝一喝，卓拄杖下座。師往姑蘇掃虎丘隆遠祖塔，道經婁東，紳衿孫逢吉、王時敏、吳偉業同監院隱山等請，就海寧寺上堂，師陞座云：「陳爛葛藤拋過一邊，巧言異語不勞拈出，別通一路出來相見，還有麼？」居士問：「世尊陞座，文殊白椎，古德頌云：『張郎沉醉一杯酒，扶醉李郎醉更深，不顧腳下水三尺，只貪步步上高岑。』今日和尚陞座、上首白椎，與黃面老子是同是別？」師云：「汝試辨驗看。」進云：「恁麼驗人，猶不知非。」師云：「不是知音莫與談。」士便喝。師云：「不怕旁觀。」士云：「忽有個漢推倒禪床、喝散大眾，也與和尚一頓作麼生？」師云：「拈一放一不是好手。」士又喝，師與一棒，士云：「什麼所在出頭來？」師云：「性命也不顧。」乃云：「若論佛法，只在迷悟之間，悟得也則行住坐臥折旋俯仰，頭頭爾、法法爾、塵塵爾、剎剎爾，無非是第一義諦，所謂治世語言、資生業等皆與實相不相違背，人人佩毘盧印，個個披解脫服，然後向作家爐鞴烹金琢玉敲骨取髓，丁一卓二橫三豎四炤用分明，收放自在，語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談，從苗辨地，拈椎豎拂見端倪，因語識人，瞬目揚眉通消息，雖在紅塵隊裏，不妨超宗異目。若無如是造詣，亂草堆頭多是觸途成滯，還有出格底道流麼？白雲盡處見青山，行人更在青山外。」喝一喝，復舉：「當時梁武帝問達磨祖師：『如何是聖諦第一義？』祖云：『廓然無聖。』帝進云：『對朕者誰？』祖云：『不識。』帝不契，祖遂渡江過魏。據達磨祖師，極則提持，使人脫聖情凡解，透脫當機、翻身格外，奈武帝執筌滯蹄，覿面蹉過，可謂遇而不遇、逢而不逢。且道達磨祖師即今在甚麼處？杖頭風月輝千古，驀路相逢若個知。」下座。上堂，僧出，師云：「昨日答汝了也。」僧云：「人人具足個個不無，是如何？」師云：「無山不帶雲。」進云：「撥草瞻風只圖見性，即今性在甚處？」師云：「又是從頭起。」乃云：「向上一著子，今日又重舉，舉得十分明，猶未敢相許。何也？即世尊住世四十九年，說法三百餘會，法門無量義海莫窮，若較之向上一著子，大似逆風揚塵，把捉不得。就五宗並峙巧言異唱，臨濟三玄三要四主四賓，雲門三句旨一字關，曹洞五位君臣三種滲漏，溈仰圓相暗機父慈子孝，法眼三界惟心萬法惟識，若較之向上一著子，亦似癩馬繫枯樁，令人無自由分。除非夙有靈骨過量底漢，向父母未生已前一覷覷破，始信古人謂『釋迦不降生

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 終難造極登峰。假如凝神定志，踴躍一番，脫卻婆娑衫子，穿著無底芒鞋，仗清風而作翅，借明月以為依，自然一舉到頂，絕沒絲毫阻滯。當此之時，千山俯伏，萬水洄漩，四海鳳龍、九州獅象悉屬家奴，飛禽走獸、魚鱉黿鼉總為擁護。到恁麼地，正好持鈯斧子砍曹山樹，提折腳鐺煮雲蒸飯。此中一段真實受用，子亦不可不知耳。示宗旭副寺示宗旭副寺。離心意識參，絕凡聖路學。參須真參，悟須實悟。真參實悟之人，為法忘身，臨大事而有以擇，臨大難而不可奪。所以楊岐百世傳聞，神鼎千秋不昧，皆是真參實悟之模範也。如宗旭禪人為同安副寺，數載殷勤，雖不及古人，亦可謂真實之人也。今山僧北行，有末後示訓之語，為你將來作藂林之輔佐。示曰：離心意識參，絕凡聖路學。未出母胎時，早已名大覺。灼然恁麼會，仍歸有卜度。一涉於絲微，垂手無所托。汝問事如何？釋迦也難捉。也難捉，三間茅屋不可居，九路僧房非著落。囑巖碧知浴囑巖碧知浴。頭目髓腦身外物，花香鳥語案中人，若能會得三玄旨，正偏坐斷絕疏親。所以道：語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談。昔日山僧在越山頂上，每日空手把鋤頭得一大受用事，三十年來未曾舉著。今朝巖碧知浴亦是其人，不妨為伊點出。昔年典座今知浴，一度恩兮一度讎，是釜是瓶都帶累，端端的的有來由。示勉習禪人示勉習禪人。快勉旃，快勉旃，時時當習釋迦言。雖然佛法無多子，也要真經有一篇。敏矣參禪還習教，殷勤習教更參禪。三乘法內堪知委，十二部中頗貫穿。兔子獲來終棄陷，魚兒歸去自忘筌。不因今日愚癡漢，那識當年大覺僊。風過喬松言外意，雲藏古洞句中玄。菩提莫謂因人學，應解菩提本自圓。示盞飯一信禪人示盞飯一信禪人。寒暑無迴避，春秋日往來。二時家常辦，缺一不成才。雖然如是，粒粒不囓著。一信禪人，可謂飯中無布，缽盂斷柄。山僧不得辜負於你，你亦不得辜負山僧。偈曰：冒雨衝風不記年，肩挑日月每盤旋。有時踏斷芒鞋後，始信功圓別有天。示純慈鐘頭示純慈鐘頭。純鋼鑄就，生鐵打成，一片慈心，古今無對。禪人自入同安以來，數年間妄緣俱削，佛法潛滋，歲月勤勞，寒暄不懼，唯知日背楞嚴玅法，夜扣幽冥洪鐘，自以精進為基，直造純清絕點，如日照世，如月照夜，孤迥迥，赤灑灑，絕承當，沒可把，五陰、六入、十二處、十八界、二十五有圓通更須彌，報如來慈益精進，方不負出家一番也。珍重！珍重！囑慧力性侍者囑慧力性侍

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 寒松，且無抽條石筍。五福則不然，無白牛可烹，無塵垢可埽，清貧非外事，澹泊何須惱？五福恁麼，你道還服得者老子口麼？」上堂。「第一句薦得，與佛祖為師；第二句薦得，與人天為師；第三句薦得，自救不了。五福即不然，第一句薦得，溼紙裏金毛；第二句薦得，單絲控玉角；第三句薦得，兔子蹋月。諸仁者還知麼？苟或不知，總是猢猻喫毛蟲。」上堂。「去年春，在天目；今年春，在五福。卻把寒梅子細看，支支牚破山頭綠。誰家釃酒賽句芒？不管子鳺啼血出。」上堂。「騎虎頭，收虎尾，第一句下明宗旨。莫有明得第一句底出來？」僧出便喝，師便打。進云：「惟此一事實，餘二則非真。」師連打，云：「落七落八了也。」問：「庭前柏樹子，意旨如何？」師云：「闍黎自道取。」進云：「趙州老漢來也。」師便打，乃云：「空中杲日，高天絕負耳之瑕；寺邊溫池，長年淨秦時之鑑。靈光獨燿，迥脫根塵，體露真常，即如如佛。大眾識麼？其或未識，待下座看。」上堂。「山青水綠，松直棘曲，喚作自然，孤負先佛。所以道：語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談。」驀顧左右，云：「分明舉似，祇是汝諸人猶欠伶俐。」上堂。「千峰峻秀，萬簇然，一室虛明，群機自露。者般時節，若是先德門下猶較些子，五福者裏未點首在。不見道：切忌動著，動著則禍生。」复舉趙州石橋話，有僧便喝，師下座，搊住云：「莫是適才喝老僧者麼？」僧擬議，師拓開便打。上堂。「年老身閒無外事，攜笻日日蹋莓苔，也知綠野情相慣，鄰曲相逢笑幾回。力倦歸來剛欲臥，椎鐘又上雨華臺。」顧視大眾，云：「者裏莫有高揖釋迦、不拜彌勒者麼？」便下座。住順寧府樹宗山善法禪院語錄住順寧府樹宗山善法禪院語錄據室。「昆池深碧，邊日含煙。地中雷复，嶺上梅鮮。此事且止，祇如古人析骨還父，析肉還母，然後見本身為眾說法。析骨析肉，不煩大眾。你道如何是本身？」時僧出作禮，師打云：「饒汝鐵額銅頭，也須七華八裂。」上堂。拈香云：「耎似棉，硬如石，開聖堂中拾來，樹宗山裏拈出，爇向盧中供養磚鏡璧和尚。」乃云：「昨日雨，今日雨，平地盆傾三尺水，許多禪客泛渺茫，帶水拖泥來山裏。者裏有箇禁忌，是甚麼禁忌聻？善法堂前切忌是非。」上堂。僧問：「灌頂之記、麟趾之祥即不問，格外超宗一句如何？」師云：「雨滴滴地。」進云：「恁麼則甘霖潤澤含青翠，白蓮村露一支春。」師云：「賴有闍黎共舉揚。」乃

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 任教明月落重臺。法執盡而見地圓，根本脫而理事徹，直窺髻裏玄珠，可別輪王至寶。如《金光明經》云：『如來言三種身：依諸伏道，起事心盡；依法斷道，依根本心盡；依最勝道，根本心盡。起事心滅故，得現化身；依根本心滅故，得顯應身；根本心滅故，得至法身。』既云教外別傳，何使提挈綱宗？假令別有規模，未免斬頭覓活。若果如是，未夢見在；若不如是，未夢見在。急須蕩盡聖凡情見，方能不滯尊貴階梯。如峰著為『秤錘落井又泥深』，斯謂藥石除而反墮膏肓之疾，鉤餌脫而復遭羅網之悲，滯十成之死句、困相似之疑城，見處既帶瓦礫，發言難印宗乘。欲識同時不識之祖父，舉步亂雲迷四野，攜笻無路透孤峰。如頌云：『翻轉青銅鏡背看。』不聞古德云：『向道莫去，歸來背父。』又何許鏡背看也？次云：『硃砂斑厚壙泥乾』，好個摩空句子，不當落在點劃場中。所云：『易分雪裏粉，難辨墨中煤。』當悟綿綿化母之機，寂寂真風一段。峰既將穿密室，何陷顧貯之泥塗，更沒文彩于琢削，豈能絕眾響而豁天真之提唱乎？宜知語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談。又云：『光生不用揩磨舊』，秪如古鏡未磨時，是個甚麼消息？末云：『漢製從來體自圓』，不見寒山道：『無物堪比倫。』峰又用製作麼？無有譬喻能喻此法，總製得圓，早已缺陷了也。將欲古之又古、深之又深，竭力摸寫，逼真得盡，不知弄巧成拙，揀點將來，料掉沒交涉。住！住！既道向亦不是、背亦不是，畢竟如何即是？」一喝，云：「鐵牛撞倒帝釋宮，百億須彌汗如雨。」峰問：「曹山立三種墮，註者言：『師凡言墮，謂混不得、類不齊。』又明安不受食，是尊貴墮。須知那邊了，卻來這邊行履，不虛此位，即墮尊貴矣。且道：曹山三墮意，畢竟是那一種？」峰著云：「從來不借雙關路，鉤鎖中間直下拋。」頌曰：這邊那邊都不得，合水和泥總不知。牛斷鼻繩湖草綠，牧童濃睡月低垂。師著云：「落日海潮夜，秋光腦後看。」頌曰：天水勿違明舊德，群龍無首殫餘知。挾類混然成錯吉，門庭三五不須垂。師荅云：「閒花野草，橫鋪古錦化春工；山色溪光，密布真風超象外。全身入荒草，徐行足跡混塵埃。脅右書半行，獨許狸奴知個事，分明頭角宛轉巴歌。故曹山有三墮之神樞，大珠剖絕向之正受。其法也，如鼎繫足，不煩輕重于其間；似月穿波，忘所合流于徹底。明安復為布置，一以折三、以三冥一，亦不另擬隨類墮之等，則尊貴墮之差殊。故云：

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 之青、水之綠，日昇月墜、魚躍鳶飛，雲生嶺頭、花發嵒畔，塵塵爾、剎剎爾，莫不各居本位。只如拈卻目前些子，將甚麼喚作佛境界？太湖三萬六千頃，月在波心幾箇知？」紫谷參頭纔出，師云：「如何是庭前柏樹子？」進云：「趙州當時錯下名言。」師云：「你又作麼生？」進云：「竹蝦蟆也解吸蒼蠅。」師下座。鐵山上座請上堂。「末後一句始到牢關。」拈拄杖，云：「奯上座一生不肯德山老漢，跛足師直欲打殺黃面瞿曇。到者裏，且道利害在甚麼？若檢點得出，一任你欺聖瞞凡、呵佛罵祖，有甚麼難？」顧左右，云：「有麼？有麼？果是金毛獅子子，三千里外見淆訛。」上堂。問：「枯木龍吟事更奇，嵒前花發許誰窺？請師別轉超方手，拈起靈山第一枝。」師云：「雨落階前滑，行人盡喫交。」進云：「疊疊巫山峰聳翠，法筵龍象盡英靈。」師云：「籜解新篁龍蛻骨，雲籠怪石虎生威。」進云：「恁麼則眉底神光吞日月，當人隨處可稱尊。」師打，云：「也須喫棒。」乃云：「大凡問荅，如鉤、如鉗，如環、如鎖，相續不斷，所謂語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談。若能如是，方可激揚法化，承紹真宗，共報佛恩，有何不可？苟非其人，不免重說偈言：將此般若殊勝勳，回施檀度獲圓滿，施者受者三輪空，而亦不作空輪想。一念頓悟超諸聖，直入如來玅境界，如來境界不思議，我今為汝說少分。法界虛空皆有盡，我此法施無有涯，一切有情及無情，同證如來無礙智。」喝一喝，云：「說到驢年去。」上堂。「夫求法者，離見聞覺知。若行見聞覺知是，則見聞覺知非求法也。」豎拂，云：「只者箇思惟分別所不能到，見聞覺知所不能及，正恁麼時又如何薦取？」揮拂，云：「薰風昨夜過林隈，吹落殘紅撩亂堆，畫閣無人香篆冷，倚欄石女淚盈腮。真堪笑，亦可哀，莫怪春歸情太薄，庭前芍藥為誰開？」上堂。「昨夜蜉蝣蟲，吞卻黃鶴峰，走向蚊子眼睫上，橫身高眠，鼓腹而歌曰：種麻得麻，種豆得豆，齋僧布施兮，因果無漏。」遂顧眾云：「爾等黃瓜茄子，還曾夢見者箇消息也未？」復喝一喝，下座。上堂。「是法住法位，世間相常住。天自高，地自厚。桃自紅，李自白。山自青，水自綠。鳧脛雖短不用續，續之則悲；鶴脛雖長不必斷，斷之則憂。長者長法身，短者短法身。且道是何意旨？最喜春來多富貴，鶯啼花笑滿林間。」薦父母師長請上堂。豎拳召眾，云：「菩提涅槃、真如佛性總在裏許。」良久，云：「菩提涅槃

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談

Senses.Explanation: The first clause lets speech carry the subtle matter without offering a fixed route. The second says the tongue speaks without settling into mere verbal statement. Later masters test whether an answer can be heard without being reduced to a reusable formula.

Senses.PreferredTarget: speech is the sprout of the mind

Occurrences.Kwic: 葉，黃梅席上獨付老盧。時緣既至，落在山僧手裏。大眾還知麼？纓絡聚中騰瑞氣，華縵影裏奪芳春。遂披衣指座，曰：此燈王座，曠劫穹隆。若是要高昇大，不觀時節。然雖恁麼，別有一般君未見，白蓮華向半天開。斂衣就座，乃曰：寶座既登，清風四起。要津把斷，凡聖俱亡。放一線道，別露風規。具眼禪人，一任施設。僧問：點鐵成金即不問，轉凡成聖事如何？師曰：棒頭有眼明如日，要識真金火裏看。僧云：數日靈禽庭畔噪，果然太守命慇懃。師曰：好個阿師，向語脈裏轉却。僧云：菩提果熟天然異，優鉢華開別是春。師曰：一語傷人，千刀攪腹。師乃曰：門裏出身易，身裏出門難。易難不到處，普請大家看。乃豎起拂子，曰：還見麼？若謂見，云何為見？見在即凡，宛同流浪。若謂不見，云何不見？行脚高士，眼在什麼處？見與不見，若為明辨？這裏徹去，三世如來、六代祖師平生關棙，瓦解冰消。苟或未然，待把少林無孔笛，為君吹起小陽春。下座。當夜小參：全機不用，同道方知；照用雙行，何人委悉？所以芭蕉和尚示眾云：你有拄杖

Senses.Explanation: Speech and language names spoken or verbal expression. Masters quote it, question it, cut it off, or place a saying within it; the word itself does not mean that language is always accepted or always rejected. Zhaozhou says that once there is speech and language there is choosing or clarity, while an unnamed monastic questioner asks Yongjue what lies beyond all speech and language. Mazu calls all speech and language the Deva school; Baizhang says speech, mountains, rivers, and the earth each turn back to oneself. Dahui says the matter cannot be fashioned through speech and language, Yuanwu says to cut it off, and Zhongfeng says opening the mouth falls at its edge.
